CMS Proposed Rule: Interoperability Standards & Prior Authorization for Drugs  Comments 1. Applicability to QHPs (Non-FFE/SHOP) It is unclear whether the rule applies to QHPs not offered on the Federally Facilitated  Exchange or SHOP. This creates uncertainty in compliance planning and resource  allocation. CMS should clarify applicability for off-exchange individual and small group  plans. 2. Interaction with State Requirements (Michigan SB 247) The relationship between the CMS proposal and existing Michigan electronic prior  authorization requirements is unclear, including whether federal requirements expand  beyond current state mandates. CMS should clarify alignment and any preemption of  state requirements. 3. Implementation Timeline The proposed timeline may not allow sufficient time for system development, vendor  coordination, and testing. Additional time may be needed to ensure readiness and  compliance. 4. Technology & Cost Burden Significant system modernization is required, including API development and workflow  redesign. These changes are expected to increase vendor costs and internal IT  investment. 5. Prior Authorization Workflow & Configuration Impact Differences in prior authorization timelines across Medicare and QHP products will  require system reconfiguration. Plans may need to separate QHP and large group  products within shared tools, increasing operational complexity. 6. Fraud, Waste & Abuse Risk Greater reliance on automated approvals may reduce documentation rigor and increase  risk of inappropriate approvals, leading to increased costs and reduced oversight. 7. Lack of Auto-Approval Clarity The rule does not define criteria for automated approvals, which may lead to  inconsistent implementation and operational risk. 8. Metric Reporting Concerns Public reporting of authorization metrics may be misinterpreted and could create  unintended incentives to alter utilization management practices. 9. Vendor Dependency Pharmacy implementation depends on PBM capabilities, while medical workflows  require additional EHR enhancements, limiting direct control over readiness.
